record.finding: Some preparations may help stress/insomnia, but other outcomes are uncertain. Rare liver injury, pregnancy/breastfeeding avoidance, thyroid/autoimmune concerns and interactions limit generic use.

record.title: Licorice Root
record.finding: Glycyrrhizin can cause serious cardiac effects, especially with prolonged/high intake or hypertension, heart/kidney conditions. Food use and specific preparations are different from unrestricted root remedies.

record.title: Kava
record.finding: Some anxiety research exists; rare severe/fatal liver injury has involved different preparations. Avoid combining with sedatives or alcohol. The profile is not a safe undosed treatment plan.

record.title: St. John’s Wort and Depression: In Depth
record.finding: Clinical findings vary. Important interactions can weaken birth-control pills and many other medicines; combining with some antidepressants can dangerously increase serotonin. Depression needs appropriate assessment.

record.title: Elderberry
record.finding: Limited preliminary respiratory research does not validate these recipes. Raw/unripe fruit and other parts contain cyanide-producing substances; cooking eliminates that toxin, but extraction in vodka is not that cooking process.

record.title: Black Cohosh
record.finding: Some extract research suggests menopause benefit; other uses are not established. Serious liver problems have been reported with labeled products, with causality uncertain; identity/contamination and hormone-sensitive conditions matter.

record.title: Tea Tree Oil
record.finding: Small amounts of topical evidence do not validate all infection claims. Tea tree oil should not be swallowed; serious neurologic toxicity can result. Skin irritation is possible.

record.publisher: Poison Control / National Capital Poison Center
record.title: Essential oils: Poisonous when misused
record.finding: Essential oils can cause skin reactions, poisoning and aspiration injury; children are particularly vulnerable. Follow actual product instructions and secure storage. Natural origin and a home patch test do not establish safety for every route.

record.publisher: Swansea Bay University Health Board, NHS Wales
record.title: Warning issued over steam remedy
record.finding: Hot-bowl steam inhalation causes scalds in adults and children; strong evidence of relief for colds/blocked noses is lacking. This constrains the bowl-and-towel procedure even though the book warns about burns and excludes children under six.

record.title: Microbiological Safety and Cosmetics
record.finding: Raw materials, water, poor processing, inadequate preservation, packaging and consumer handling can contaminate cosmetics. A clean jar, shaking or refrigeration does not itself validate a preservation system.

record.title: Shelf Life and Expiration Dating of Cosmetics
record.finding: Shelf life depends on formulation, packaging, handling and storage. Water, consumer contamination and degraded preservatives matter; drug products such as sunscreens require stability testing. No book recipe shelf life is confirmed.

record.title: Homemade sunscreens are not proven effective
record.finding: Homemade sunscreen does not undergo the testing needed to establish SPF, water resistance and shelf life. Ingredient presence and kitchen mixing do not prove UV protection.

record.title: Preventing Mosquito Bites
record.finding: CDC/EPA recommend EPA-registered repellents used as labeled. Effectiveness of nonregistered natural mixtures is unknown; this recipe has no established protection interval.

record.title: Find the Repellent that is Right for You
record.finding: Registration indicates submitted technical safety/effectiveness information. Use product-specific mosquito/tick protection and label instructions; a familiar plant name is not product registration.

record.title: Home Oral Care
record.finding: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste. Coconut oil, clay, salt and essential oils do not establish equivalent anticaries protection for this fluoride-free recipe.

record.title: Synthetic Substances in Crop Production
record.finding: Organic production permits listed synthetic and many nonsynthetic substances, including pesticides. Organic sourcing is not a pesticide-free or clinically effective guarantee.

record.title: 4VAC5-30-50 Flowers, plants, minerals, etc.
record.finding: Virginia state parks restrict plant removal; a scientific-collecting permit is a specified route, with a personal-use exception for edible fruits, berries, fungi and nuts. This is not blanket permission to uproot medicinal plants.

record.title: Herb Culture and Use
record.locator: Site; indexed excerpt, direct URL unavailable
record.finding: Primary indexed text describes species/habitat-specific light, drainage and pH needs, often six to eight hours sun. Direct page returned404, so this is excerpt-only context, not verified gardening instructions.

record.title: How to Safely Make Infused Oils
record.finding: Primary indexed text distinguishes fresh herbs/garlic and botulism risk, tested acidification and refrigerated alternatives. Dried herbs are different, but the book’s universal one-year room-storage claim is not validated. Direct access403.

record.title: Foods and Drinks to Avoid or Limit
record.finding: Do not give honey before twelve months because of infant botulism. The book excludes under-two-year-olds, a stricter restriction; it does not omit the warning. Neither threshold validates its child syrup dose.

record.title: Symphyti radix
record.finding: The specific comfrey-root preparation assessment concerns adult short-term minor sprains/bruises, with quantified pyrrolizidine-alkaloid limits. It does not approve arbitrary homemade oils, broken-skin use, fracture treatment or osteoporosis treatment.

record.title: Peppermint Oil
record.finding: Limited adult IBS evidence concerns enteric-coated capsules; leaves, unformulated oil and skin routes are different. Reflux/irritation can occur. Do not apply menthol-containing peppermint oil to an infant or small child’s face.

record.title: Ginger
record.finding: Some evidence concerns pregnancy-associated nausea and oral supplements, not every nausea cause or food/skin preparation. Topical ginger has not been shown helpful for knee osteoarthritis; interactions and irritation matter.

record.title: Garlic
record.finding: Some supplement cardiovascular effects are modest; immune research is limited. Fresh raw garlic can cause skin irritation/burns, and supplements may increase bleeding risk, particularly with relevant medicines or surgery.

record.title: Aloe Vera
record.finding: Topical gel, latex and whole-leaf oral extracts differ. Some topical burn evidence exists, but oral latex can cause GI effects and leaf extracts have liver concerns. This does not validate undifferentiated aloe uses.

record.title: Turmeric
record.finding: Evidence and absorption vary by preparation; promising early findings are not definitive. Highly bioavailable formulations have caused liver injury; supplement use is different from culinary seasoning.

record.title: Detoxes and Cleanses
record.finding: There is no compelling research supporting detox diets for eliminating toxins. Suspected toxic-metal exposure requires qualified assessment rather than assumed cilantro chelation; this source does not test the book’s specific herb.

record.publisher: Wiley / Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics
record.title: Development of multiplex pyrosequencing for HLA-B*57:01 screening using single nucleotide polymorphism haplotype
record.locator: Publisher indexed article text; ordinary landing page403
record.finding: The publisher’s indexed article identifies Sankuntaw and colleagues,2014,39:545–550 and a pharmacogenetic assay. Book PDF75 assigns that DOI to Gowda et al., an Andrographis review,39:497–508. This is a bibliographic mismatch; no clinical conclusions from the assay are applied here.

record.publisher: University of Pretoria, research authors’ institution
record.title: Peer Reviewed Publications
record.finding: Institutional list identifies DOI10.1016/j.jep.2016.03.036 as Moyo et al., in-vitro Plasmodium gametocyte study,2016;185:235–242. Book PDF74 assigns it to Akhtar/Bhatti/Sarwar adaptogenic plants,187:122–135. This checks identity only.

record.title: Colds, Flu, and Complementary Health Approaches
record.finding: Evidence for echinacea and similar cold products varies by species, plant part and preparation; one preparation’s research does not establish another’s effect. No mixed home tincture or syrup here is validated.

record.title: Part95 SubpartB — FRS
record.finding: FRS has22 shared channels,including467MHz channels8–14;channel3 is462.6125MHz. Limits are2W ERP except0.5W ERP on8–14,with a nonremovable integral antenna. A service-authorized radio is required; price or a programmable frequency is not authorization.

record.title: Part95 SubpartD — CBRS
record.finding: CB has40 authorized channels; AM/FM carrier limit4W and SSB12W PEP. Channel9 is restricted to emergency/traveler assistance,without a guaranteed listener. Antenna rule uses60ft above ground OR20ft above building/tree,whichever is higher,plus aviation limits. Plain-language,certification and modification rules also apply.

record.title: Part95 SubpartJ — MURS
record.finding: Five specific VHF channels include151.940MHz; transmitter output is at most2W. MURS has its own antenna,bandwidth and equipment rules; its height wording must not be replaced by the book’s incorrect combined CB caps. No fixed household range follows.

record.title: Part95 SubpartE — GMRS
record.finding: GMRS requires an individual license,with specified family eligibility and certified equipment.462.6000MHz is a main channel. Hidden-meaning coded messages are prohibited; assigned callsign identification is required,including15-minute intervals during longer series. FRS interoperability does not erase the GMRS operator’s requirements.

record.title: Part97 — Amateur Radio Service
record.finding: Privileges depend on license,class,frequency,mode and power. Messages encoded to obscure meaning are prohibited except specified exceptions. Assigned identification is required at end and at least every10minutes. Current60m rules include5.3515–5.3665MHz with9.15W ERP,not a generic high-power channel. Emergency provisions concern immediate safety/need,not wholesale suspension of rules.

record.title: Part95 SubpartA — General personal-radio rules
record.finding: Eligible compliant CB/FRS/MURS operation is authorized by rule without an individual license; other services such as GMRS require one. Equipment-certification restrictions include voice-obscuring features. Rules differ by service; no blanket claim that every manual code on every radio service is illegal is made.

record.title: NOAA Weather Radio FAQ
record.locator: How can I listen; frequencies; range
record.finding: NWR requires receiver coverage of seven VHF weather frequencies162.400–162.550MHz. A plain broadcast-AM/FM receiver is insufficient unless it also has weather-band capability. Terrain,antenna and actual local transmitter coverage matter.

record.title: Make a Plan
record.finding: Discuss responsibilities and practice the plan. Arrange near-home and outside-neighborhood meeting places and an out-of-area contact; carry contact details on paper and phones. This supports planning,not guaranteed radio reach or mandatory travel through hazards.

record.title: SP800-63B-4 — Authentication and Authenticator Management
record.finding: Replay resistance depends on transaction freshness; repeating the same secret output is not replay-resistant. Apply this as a technical analogy to overheard fixed radio phrases,not a claim this digital-identity standard certifies a family voice protocol.

record.title: A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography, version0.6
record.locator: Theorem2.2, printed p.9 / PDF25; sections3.3.1–3.3.2,printed pp.52–54 / PDF68–70
record.finding: A uniformly random secret pad used once gives perfect secrecy for fixed-length messages under the defined model. Reuse and key handling matter; the pad does not itself authenticate messages,and message length/traffic exposure remain separate.

record.title: Set and manage disappearing messages
record.finding: Disappearing messages do not prevent a recipient recording a screen with another camera. A retention setting is not proof of anonymity,secure endpoints or an offline delivery path.

record.title: Privacy Policy
record.finding: The developer describes account privacy and no required phone number,but also seed-node IP visibility and mobile-operating-system telemetry limitations. Policy/design statements are not an independent security audit or guaranteed untraceability.

record.title: Operators Privacy Policy and Conditions of Use
record.finding: The developer describes queue/relay delivery,server-held undelivered messages and device/push-notification privacy boundaries. No-user-ID design is different from no infrastructure or universal invisibility.

record.title: Resilience Against Electromagnetic Pulses
record.finding: EMP can disrupt,degrade or damage equipment and infrastructure. This2019policy statement does not establish that every phone,tower,antenna or stored byte must be destroyed,nor certify an improvised shield.

record.title: What to Do to Protect Yourself During a Power Outage
record.finding: Generators need outdoor placement away from building openings and CO precautions. A radio load does not make indoor combustion safe or validate the book’s unspecified backup installation.

record.title: 1926.441 Batteries and battery charging
record.finding: Unsealed batteries require ventilation and protection from explosive gas/electrolyte hazards. This construction-workplace standard illustrates battery hazards; it is not represented as the governing design code for this household.

record.title: Downed Power Lines
record.finding: Treat downed lines as energized and dangerous; electricity can travel through associated conductive materials. An outage is not proof utility wires/poles are safe to touch or use as supports.

record.title: Damage prevention — Video Presentations and transcripts
record.finding: Safe excavation requires utility-location and damage-prevention procedures. The book’s casual buried-wire slit is not a site/legal/safe-route assessment. No universal claim overriding statutory exemptions is made.

record.title: Dig With Care
record.locator: Positive Response; Hand Digging; private-utilities link
record.finding: Wait for positive response and follow marking/hand-dig precautions; shallow work can still encounter hazards. Private facilities may require separate identification. No cable trench or location was cleared.

record.title: Part90 — Private Land Mobile Radio Services
record.finding: 155.160MHz appears in the Public Safety Pool with eligibility/use limits. Licensees control permissible operations and authorized users. A book label or amateur license does not turn it into a general public helicopter-calling channel.

record.title: Part80 — Stations in the Maritime Services
record.finding: Channel16 at156.800MHz is distress,safety and calling;72 at156.625MHz is noncommercial intership. Associated-ship use from adjacent shore exists under specific conditions,not a blanket inland family channel authorization.

record.title: 47CFR2.1 — Terms and definitions
record.finding: Radio direction-finding uses received radio waves to determine a station/object direction. Emission can support location techniques; no5–10second invisibility window or universal fast location accuracy is established.

record.title: Band Plan
record.locator: 2 Meters; voluntary band plan,not federal rule
record.finding: The voluntary US amateur band plan identifies146.52MHz as the national simplex calling frequency. It is not a continuously staffed emergency/chat net; actual activity and local coordination vary.

record.title: Communication Equipment student handout B191716
record.locator: Indexed excerpt only; full access blocked
record.finding: Primary indexed handout identifies TA-312/PT and two D-cell batteries. FullPDF access403; no claimed wet/dry distance,used-unit condition or emergency sound-powered configuration was independently validated here.

record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.finding: Use suitable food-grade containers and safe water; never repurpose toxic-chemical containers. Baseline at least one gallon per person per day for three days, with a two-week aim and additional needs. This does not make an arbitrary bathtub potable.

record.title: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
record.finding: Boiling and disinfection address germs, not fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactive contamination. Follow actual advisory/source assessment and product directions; a tablet or filter is not a universal treatment.

record.title: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
record.finding: Keep refrigerator/freezer doors closed and use time/temperature rules. An unopened refrigerator generally keeps food safe four hours; discard unsafe perishables and foods exposed to contamination. Taste does not establish safety.

record.title: Make a Plan
record.finding: Discuss responsibilities, meeting places, out-of-area contacts and evacuation arrangements, then practice. Preserve paper/phone contact information. Supports household planning, not a universal 48/72-hour departure window.

record.title: FAQ: Rules of war
record.locator: Civilian objects; hospitals/schools; explosive weapons; sieges; corridors
record.finding: Civilians and civilian objects are protected; hospital protection has specific conditions. Armed presence does not erase all attack constraints. Wide-area explosive effects can extend beyond a target. Humanitarian corridors require coordination; legal protection is not guaranteed physical safety.

record.title: Frequently asked questions on the missing
record.locator: Central Tracing Agency; support for families
record.finding: The ICRC and Family Links Network help prevent separation, reconnect families and search for missing persons. Actual tracing procedures and access depend on context; no book checkpoint script guarantees release.

record.title: Psychological first aid: Guide for field workers
record.locator: Publication overview,2011; not a new clinical guideline
record.finding: The overview describes humane, supportive and practical help that respects dignity, culture and ability. This supports social support, not the book’s informant-detection rules or a promise of psychological recovery.

record.title: Food and Nutrition Information Center
record.finding: Nutrition needs have life-stage and individual dimensions; DRI tools and food-composition data are available. Fat provides about nine calories per gram, not a statement that every100ml of oil weighs100g.

record.title: Emergency food assistance standard
record.locator: Primary indexed excerpt only; full body blocked
record.finding: Indexed primary-source excerpt describes an initial population food-basket planning value around2100kcal/person/day with context adjustments. Full body required a JavaScript robot check. It is not used to prescribe an individual intake or verify starvation thresholds.

record.title: Guidelines for Personal Hygiene During an Emergency
record.finding: Use soap/water and scrub at least20seconds. Keep wounds clean/covered; avoid contaminated water and seek care for redness, swelling or discharge. Use clean water for teeth and follow local water advice.

record.title: 2024 Guidelines for First Aid
record.finding: First aid must match skills and seek further care. Direct pressure is the mainstay for life-threatening bleeding; uncontrolled extremity bleeding can require a tourniquet. Thermal burns need prompt cooling;5–20minutes may be reasonable, with child hypothermia monitoring. Serious burns and smoke inhalation require professional care. This does not validate a complete home medical protocol.

record.title: Cholera outbreaks
record.finding: If packets are unavailable, the stated household mixture is1litre safe water,6teaspoons sugar and half a teaspoon salt. Packets must follow their label. Rehydration accompanies prompt care; severe diarrhoea, insufficient fluid intake, confusion or marked weakness require urgent help. This is not a complete pediatric dosing regimen.

record.title: Garlic: Usefulness and Safety
record.finding: Fresh raw garlic on skin can cause severe irritation and chemical burns. Oral forms can cause adverse effects; supplements can increase bleeding and interact with medicines. Lab antimicrobial activity does not establish a safe wound treatment.

record.title: Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do’s and Don’ts
record.finding: Use antibiotics only when indicated and exactly as prescribed; do not share, save leftovers or take another person’s prescription. Wrong treatment can delay care and cause harm. No general amoxicillin-first emergency regimen is endorsed.

record.title: The right respirator and proper fit can reduce wildfire-smoke exposure
record.finding: Wet/dry cloth and paper masks do not protect against fine wildfire-smoke particles. Avoid exposure first; properly fitted NIOSH particulate respirators have limits, including fit. This is particle guidance, not protection from all combustion gases or explosive dust hazards.

record.title: Burns and scalds
record.finding: Cool promptly under running water for20minutes and cover after cooling without wrapping cling film around a limb. Severe burns need hospital care. UK emergency numbers are not copied into a Virginia household plan.

record.title: Code of Virginia §54.1-3410
record.finding: The statute regulates pharmacist dispensing pursuant to prescriptions and specified exceptions. It is not a general authorization for household prescription-drug barter. Consult actual pharmacy/prescriber arrangements; this is not a full legal opinion.

record.title: Before and After the Storm — Private Wells and Onsite Sewage Systems
record.finding: Outages/flooding can interrupt well pumps and onsite sewage systems; contaminated wells need assessment/disinfection/testing and local health advice. This page concerns wells/onsite systems, not clearance to flush a failed municipal sewer or certify the irrigation well as potable.

record.title: Make a Plan
record.finding: Primary indexed excerpt describes household contacts, medical needs, evacuation and shelter planning. Full body returned403; no verified record relies on inaccessible content.

record.title: Natural Toxins in Food
record.finding: Raw/undercooked beans can contain harmful lectin; proper soaking and boiling matter. Natural food toxins also occur in some plants/fungi. This is not proof that arbitrary boiled greens are safe.

record.title: Reducing Microbial Food Safety Hazards in Seed for Sprouting
record.finding: The reviewed guidance landing-page introduction identifies continuing foodborne-illness outbreaks linked to raw/lightly cooked sprouts. This industry guidance is not a ban on growing cress or proof that every seedling is eaten as a sprout.

record.title: Candle Fire Safety
record.finding: Open flames introduce fire hazards; USFA recommends flashlights for power outages. This constrains safe lighting choices, not the book’s unverified barter demand.

record.title: About Sepsis
record.finding: Sepsis is a life-threatening emergency that can quickly cause organ damage and death without fast treatment. A days-long wound-to-systemic-illness window cannot be assumed safe.

record.title: Oral Hygiene
record.finding: Brushing with fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between teeth protect oral health. A saltwater rinse does not supply the same preventive measures or establish abscess treatment.

record.title: Ibuprofen
record.finding: Warnings include cardiovascular/GI risks, kidney disease, interactions and pregnancy restrictions. For children with inadequate drinking or fluid loss, consult their clinician. Actual product labeling and patient-specific suitability remain essential.

record.title: 2024 First Aid Guidelines
record.finding: First aid is limited by training and must seek further care. Supports scene safety, consent, direct pressure and appropriate escalation. Addresses chest wounds, spinal motion restriction, burns, anaphylaxis, oxygen, snakebite and fractures; topic-specific constraints are not a complete household clinical protocol.

record.title: 2025 Adult Basic Life Support
record.finding: Activate emergency response, use CPR/AED promptly, avoid delay from lay pulse checks and blind finger sweeps. Adult compression rate100–120/min and depth at least5cm while avoiding more than6cm. Severe responsive-adult choking uses5back blows alternating5abdominal thrusts, with specified exceptions.

record.title: 2025 Pediatric Basic Life Support
record.finding: Age, size and responder context change CPR and choking care. Infant compression uses one-hand or two-thumb encircling technique on an appropriate support; not arbitrary back-in-hand compressions. Breaths matter in pediatric arrest and infants do not receive abdominal thrusts.

record.title: First Aid for Seizures
record.locator: How to help; when to call; what to avoid
record.finding: Protect from surrounding hazards, stay, time the seizure and seek help for specified emergencies. Do not restrain, put objects in the mouth or give food/drink until fully alert.

record.title: Stop the Bleed just-in-time guide
record.finding: The primary guide explicitly says not to loosen or remove a bleeding-control tourniquet while awaiting professional care. Application needs suitable equipment/technique and monitoring; not a periodic-release schedule.

record.title: First Aid for Poisoning,2024
record.finding: Do not give activated charcoal as routine swallowed-poison first aid. Identify substance, time and amount and obtain case-specific advice. Route-specific decontamination differs; unconsciousness, seizure or inability to breathe requires emergency services.

record.title: Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do’s and Don’ts
record.finding: Antibiotics treat selected bacterial infections, not viruses. Use only as prescribed; do not share, save leftovers or take another person’s prescription. Broad symptom lists do not select the right medicine.

record.title: Cholera outbreaks
record.finding: The household fallback when ORS packets unavailable is1litre safe water,6teaspoons sugar and half a teaspoon salt. Packets follow their actual directions. Rehydration begins during illness; severe diarrhoea, inadequate intake, confusion or marked weakness need urgent care.

record.title: Personal Hygiene During an Emergency
record.finding: Handwashing and clean/covered wounds reduce contamination. Use appropriate safe water and obtain care for concerning infection signs. No surgical sterility or permission to probe deep wounds follows.

record.title: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
record.finding: Boiling/disinfection target germs, not all toxic chemicals, fuel or radioactive contamination. Match source and local advisory; cooled boiled water is not automatically sterile surgical fluid.

record.title: About Sepsis
record.finding: Sepsis is a life-threatening emergency. Without fast treatment, it can quickly cause tissue damage, organ failure and death. Home antibiotics and oral fluids do not establish a complete treatment plan.

record.title: Malaria vaccines:RTS,S and R21
record.finding: WHO recommends two malaria vaccines for children in malaria-endemic settings as part of comprehensive control. This contradicts no malaria vaccine exists, without making vaccination a routine Virginia family/traveler recommendation.

record.title: Yellow Book2026:Malaria
record.finding: Prophylaxis is destination/resistance/patient specific. Mefloquine can be recommended during pregnancy for chloroquine-resistant areas; psychiatric/seizure contraindications remain. Do not mix prevention and acute-treatment drug regimens.

record.title: Clinical Care of RMSF
record.finding: Doxycycline is first-line for suspected RMSF across ages, including young children and pregnancy under clinical care. Early treatment matters; other agents are not interchangeable just because the book lists them.

record.title: Treating Typhoid Fever and Paratyphoid Fever
record.finding: Timely appropriate antibiotics reduce complications/death. Untreated illness can persist weeks/months and become fatal; resistance can determine therapy. Do not wait for presumed self-cure.

record.title: Clinical Guidance for Ebola Disease
record.finding: FDA-approved treatments/vaccine exist for disease caused by Ebola virus, not all orthoebolaviruses. Suspected disease needs public-health notification, specific PPE/testing and professional care; not generic household symptomatic management.

record.title: Treatment of Low Blood Sugar
record.finding: Conscious patients who can swallow use appropriate fast carbohydrate and reassessment; young children may need different amounts. Severe episodes can need prescribed glucagon and emergency help. Oral glucose is not safe for an unconscious person.

record.title: Potassium Iodide in Radiation Emergencies
record.finding: KI has a narrow radioactive-iodine thyroid-protection role when officials/clinicians instruct. It does not protect against all radiation or establish treatment for an unexplained thyroid lump.

record.title: Frequently Asked Questions on Potassium Iodide
record.finding: Seafood/shellfish allergy does not necessarily imply iodine or KI hypersensitivity. KI indication, actual sensitivities and thyroid/other contraindications need medical/public-health assessment.

record.title: Understanding Blood Pressure Readings
record.finding: Normal adult BP is below120/80;140systolic or90diastolic is stage2hypertension, not a healthy default. Measurement, repeat assessment and symptoms matter; no blanket one-dose-until-normal plan follows.

record.title: Disinfection and Sterilization Recommendations
record.finding: Critical surgical instruments require validated sterilization, compatible equipment and process controls. Cleaning, disinfection, boiling/flame/alcohol improvisation are not interchangeable proof of surgical sterility. Healthcare guidance is applied as a limit, not a home operating-room design.

record.title: Code of Virginia54.1-3410
record.finding: Prescription dispensing has legal requirements and specific exceptions. Disaster language does not confer blanket permission to scavenge, possess or administer any prescription drug. Arrange lawful prescriber/pharmacy continuity.

record.title: Animal Bite
record.finding: Wash animal-bite wounds and seek proper medical attention; report exposures to local authorities/health departments for rabies assessment. Antibiotic ointment is not rabies prevention.

record.title: Wound Management to Prevent Tetanus
record.finding: Assess wound type and vaccination history for vaccine and, when indicated, tetanus immune globulin. Antibiotics are not recommended solely to prevent tetanus. Established tetanus requires medical treatment beyond a household antibiotic list.

record.title: About Bacterial Meningitis
record.finding: Meningitis involves the protective lining of brain/spinal cord; serious bacterial disease needs immediate medical evaluation/treatment. Transmission and contact prophylaxis depend on the cause and exposure, not every contact receiving an arbitrary antibiotic.

record.title: Eating,Diet and Nutrition for Kidney Stones
record.finding: Prevention depends on stone type and actual health conditions. Adequate dietary calcium can help prevent some stones; blanket dietary calcium restriction is not appropriate. Fluid advice must account for individual health.

record.title: Insulin Storage and Switching in an Emergency
record.finding: Follow actual insulin product storage and clinician instructions. Heat/freezing and product differences matter. Switching ideally needs medical supervision/close glucose monitoring; an unspecified hefty stockpile or symptom-based dose is not a plan.

record.title: Don’t Be Tempted to Use Expired Medicines
record.finding: Expiry and labeled storage matter; after expiry there is no guarantee of safety/effectiveness. FDA advises against expired use; government-controlled stability extensions do not establish a household medicine’s condition.

record.title: SALT Mass Casualty Triage Algorithm
record.finding: SALT separates immediate, delayed, minimal, expectant and dead categories with defined assessment/intervention/resource steps. An abbreviated color list or three priorities is not complete trained mass-casualty triage. Expectant and dead must not be conflated.

record.title: Using Alcohol to Relieve Your Pain
record.finding: Alcohol pain relief has harmful consequences and interactions: acetaminophen liver toxicity, aspirin gastric bleeding and opioid sedation/overdose risks. It is not a household emergency analgesic recommendation.

record.title: Garlic
record.finding: Raw topical garlic can cause irritation/chemical burns and oral/supplement forms can interact with medicines. It is not a validated interchangeable replacement for ibuprofen or wound treatment.

record.title: First aid:Act fast
record.finding: Do not induce vomiting. First aid depends on substance and route; contact poison specialists and emergency services for serious symptoms. Some caustic ingestions permit limited water/milk only when awake, not convulsing and able to swallow.

record.title: Foreign object in the skin:First aid
record.finding: Deeply embedded, very painful or concerning objects need prompt professional help; do not attempt deep removal. Padding around a significant embedded object can protect it without direct pressure on it.

record.title: Ten Essentials
record.finding: Outdoor essentials include navigation, extra clothing, illumination, first aid, nutrition, hydration and emergency shelter. Match the activity and conditions; the list is not a demonstrated 72-hour family capacity.

record.title: Outdoor Emergency Plan
record.locator: Before trip; group travel; lost response
record.finding: Practice equipment and the plan, use a mapped meeting location, stay together and use designated trails. If lost, assess safe retracing first; when seeking rescue, report location and stay unless immediately threatened. Visibility and signaling help rescuers.

record.title: Water Treatment Options When Hiking, Camping, or Traveling
record.finding: Clear streams may contain germs. Boiling targets germs; filtration and disinfection are not interchangeable. Follow product instructions, account for organism coverage and iodine contraindications. Chemical/toxin/radioactive contamination requires another source, not boiling or disinfection.

record.title: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
record.finding: Flowing surface water is generally preferred to stagnant water, but still requires treatment. Boiling/disinfection do not eliminate metals, salts or most chemicals. Flooded wells need appropriate disinfection/testing. No site is certified potable by this page.

record.title: Resolve to be Ready for Emergencies
record.locator: Make a Resolution; Get Tech Ready
record.finding: Plan a safe meeting place, evacuation routes and an out-of-town contact. Maintain supplies and documents, receive local alerts and have device backup power. This is general planning, not a personalized route.

record.publisher: New Jersey Office of Emergency Management
record.title: Evacuation
record.locator: How do I evacuate; Go Kit; official alerts
record.finding: Official instructions inform evacuation routes, shelter and transport. A go kit must consider prescriptions, disabilities, childcare, identification and carrying capacity. Routes and transit arrangements are jurisdiction- and incident-specific.

record.title: Dispose of Waste Properly
record.finding: Check local rules and facilities. Some places require waste pack-out systems; where catholes are appropriate, NPS gives 6–8 inches and 200 feet from water, trails and camps. Pack out toilet paper. Concealment or generic double-bagging is not a complete sanitation plan.

record.title: The Skinny on Soap
record.locator: Soap impacts and distance from water
record.finding: Biodegradable soap still harms waters. Do not introduce soap into a stream or lake; wash away from water and minimize use. This constrains bathing/laundry, not proof of scent elimination.

record.title: Bear Safety: Storing Food
record.finding: Pack out scraps and garbage and treat attractants as food. Site-specific food-storage requirements may call for lockers or bear-resistant containers. Low odor, a resealable bag or a buried cache alone is not wildlife protection.

record.title: Novelty Makeup
record.finding: Use products intended for the skin and follow location-specific label warnings, especially around eyes. Contaminated products and irritation matter. Outdoor mud or arbitrary paint is not endorsed as face makeup.

record.title: Can Thermal Imaging See Through Walls?
record.finding: Typical thermal imagers observe surface radiation: ordinary walls, glass, metal and tree trunks do not offer direct see-through views; surfaces can warm or reflect. Smoke and darkness do not necessarily prevent imaging. This does not validate any personal concealment system.

record.title: Can Thermal Imaging See Through Fog and Rain?
record.finding: Range depends on detector band, atmosphere, target contrast and distance. Dense fog can limit infrared as severely as visible imaging; rain may significantly reduce contrast. No universal fog-penetration or safe-distance guarantee follows.

record.title: General Information & Hunting Regulations
record.finding: Blaze-color requirements apply to specified hunters and accompanying people, with season/activity exceptions. They are not a universal law for every hiker. Visibility and lawful land access must be assessed before adopting camouflage advice.

record.title: State Park Rules and Regulations
record.finding: Official indexed excerpt prohibits damaging or gathering park plants/materials outside limited permissions and says to use dumpsters or pack trash out. Full-page open returned 403; this excerpt is a constraint only, never verified support.

record.publisher: City of Virginia Beach Emergency Management
record.title: Evacuating
record.finding: Virginia Beach publishes designated hurricane routes and warns the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel is not one. Road and ramp controls illustrate why access changes need official local information. Do not use this city-specific page as this household’s actual route.

record.title: Cameras, Safes, and Smart Habits: Residential Burglary Prevention Tips
record.locator: Basics; valuables; camera placement; security assessment
record.finding: Supports locks, reinforced strike plates, secured garages, maintained sightlines, motion lighting, protected valuables and thoughtful camera coverage. It offers residential assessments; no percentage or post-collapse deterrence guarantee is supplied.

record.title: False Alarm and Security Systems
record.locator: False alarm prevention; power interruptions; user training
record.finding: Outages, low batteries, weather and user errors can trigger false alarms. Maintain contacts/batteries and teach users operation/cancellation. Local registration and response rules apply; backup power is finite, not a promise of instant police arrival.

record.title: 13VAC5-52-220: Means of Egress
record.finding: Required exits and rescue openings must remain usable under the applicable building code. Bars/grilles over required rescue openings must release from inside without keys/tools or excessive force. Do not infer every window is a required opening or every residential lock has the same rule.

record.title: Model Jury Instructions — Criminal, Release26
record.finding: Instruction33.800 describes without-fault self-defense in terms of reasonable imminent fear of death/great bodily harm and no more force than reasonably necessary.33.810 has different at-fault conditions. This is a legal limit, not a complete opinion on a household incident or permission to shoot over property.

record.title: Code18.2-51: Bodily injury with intent to maim, disable or kill
record.finding: Virginia criminalizes specified malicious or unlawful bodily injury with the stated intent. Reviewer applies this as a warning against injurious traps; the statute is not a trap-design rule or a complete determination of liability in a hypothetical disaster.

record.title: Preventing Firearm Injury and Death
record.finding: Hiding or placing firearms out of reach is not secure storage. Locked storage helps prevent unauthorized access; unloaded locked guns and separately secured ammunition are emphasized. This does not validate firearm selection, use-of-force tactics or a weapon-filled family refuge.

record.title: How To Secure Your Home Security Cameras
record.finding: Connected cameras require protected accounts/networks, updates, encryption, appropriate permissions and consideration of remote-viewing privacy. Convenience is not immunity from compromise or outage.

record.title: Hold Mail Service
record.finding: USPS offers eligible-address mail holding for3–30days, with identity verification for online requests. This verifies availability of the service, not crime reduction or indefinite holding.

record.title: Safety and Security Window Films brochure
record.finding: Properly applied films may retain shards and delay intrusion under stated conditions; manufacturer disclaims bullet resistance and guaranteed prevention of injury or entry. Product and installation selection need professional assessment.

record.publisher: Office of the Federal Register / CPSC
record.title: 16CFR1201.1: Architectural glazing scope
record.finding: Safety-glazing requirements apply to specified architectural products including doors and patio-type sliding doors. Scope, material, manufacture and application matter. This does not mandate acrylic in every window or establish burglary/ballistic resistance.

record.title: Testing and Certification for Bullet-Resistant Materials
record.finding: UL752 evaluates specified barrier materials/assemblies for penetration, fragments and spalling under defined ballistic conditions. No household sandbag pile or ordinary metal door becomes rated merely by material name; no book assembly was tested.

record.title: What to Expect
record.finding: Contact before digging or driving landscaping/fence supports, wait for the applicable process and account for private utilities that member locates do not mark. This constrains lawful fencing and burial projects, not injurious traps.

record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.finding: Home-filled drinking water needs suitable containers, dates, rotation and cool storage away from sunlight/toxic substances. A hiding place or buried container does not prove safe water or household coverage.

record.title: Expiration Dates — Questions and Answers
record.finding: Labeled storage and expiry matter. Temperature, humidity and light affect stability; controlled federal-stockpile extensions do not establish a household product’s condition. Buried or concealed medicines are not automatically safely stored.

record.title: Carbon Monoxide Hazard: Using a Generator
record.finding: Generator exhaust can kill; never run a generator indoors, in a garage or carport. Theft protection or anchoring must not override ventilation and safe operating location.

record.title: Euphorbia milii — Crown of Thorns
record.finding: Latex sap can injure skin/eyes and ingestion causes irritation; keep away from children/pets. This is one species associated with the common name, not proof of the author’s botanical intent or Virginia outdoor suitability.

record.title: Japanese Barberry
record.finding: Japanese barberry is identified as invasive in Virginia regions and thorns can injure pedestrians. The book’s unspecific barberry label does not identify a cultivar/species; do not treat all barberries as identical.

record.title: Residential Fences and Walls
record.finding: Fence height/location and certain permits depend on lot, use and exceptions. This county summary illustrates local constraints only; household jurisdiction, parcel and lawful fence design are unknown.

record.title: What to do During a Tornado
record.finding: Tornado shelter choices favor a basement, safe room or suitable interior room away from windows; a shed is not a substitute. Intrusion hiding places are not automatically weather shelters.

record.title: Riot Control Agents
record.locator: Background; signs and symptoms; closed settings
record.finding: Pepper spray and related irritants can injure eyes/airways/skin; severe and potentially fatal effects can occur with major/prolonged exposure, especially enclosed settings. Non-lethal is not a harmlessness guarantee.

record.title: Resolve to be Ready for Emergencies
record.finding: Supports neighbor communication, emergency planning, alerts, documents and device backup power. It does not endorse vigilantism, armed neighborhood control or assuming all responders are absent.

record.title: Powers and duties of Governor
record.finding: Virginia specifies emergency powers and conditions. The operative order and jurisdiction determine actual restrictions.

record.title: Ex parte Milligan
record.finding: The ruling addresses military trial of a civilian where civil courts were open.

record.title: Making Water Safe in an Emergency
record.locator: Making Water Safe in an Emergency
record.finding: Boiling or disinfection cannot make water contaminated by fuels or toxic chemicals safe.

record.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics
record.finding: Do not operate portable camping stoves indoors.

record.title: Preventing Hypothermia
record.finding: Warm layers help reduce cold exposure. Shivering and confusion are warning signs. Hypothermia is a medical emergency.

record.title: Declaration of local emergency
record.finding: Subsection C describes conditional local authority over specified commodities and retains mandatory constitutional requirements.

record.title: Growing Plants in Space
record.finding: Actual controlled growing systems specify plant environment and resource delivery.

record.title: Virginia’s Home Garden Vegetable Planting Guide
record.locator: Virginia’s Home Garden Vegetable Planting Guide
record.finding: Regional crop tables include cool-season windows for kale and warm-season windows for okra.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Ensuring Safe Canned Foods
record.finding: Acidity and a tested process matter. Low-acid vegetables require pressure canning unless a tested acidified recipe applies.

record.title: Potato plant poisoning
record.finding: Green potatoes and sprouts can contain toxic glycoalkaloids.

record.title: Poisonous Plants in Vermont
record.finding: False hellebore can be mistaken for ramps.

record.title: Emergency water supply
record.locator: Water amounts, containers, cleaning and rotation
record.support_scope: At least one US gallon per person daily for three days; try two weeks. Suitable containers and six-month home-filled-water replacement. Extra needs can increase quantities.

record.title: Making water safe
record.support_scope: Safe water sources, clarification versus germ treatment, and limits for fuel/toxic-chemical contamination. CDC boiling elevation boundary is 6500 feet.

record.title: Emergency disinfection of drinking water
record.support_scope: One-minute rolling boil; three minutes above 5000 feet. Boiling/disinfection does not remove salts, metals and many chemicals. Metric altitude parenthetical on the page is inconsistent; this core uses feet only.

record.title: Testing well water
record.locator: Test panel, certified laboratory and health department advice
record.support_scope: Testing and interpretation depend on local hazards. A test panel does not establish pump availability, plumbing compliance or a permanent safety guarantee.

record.title: Food safety after an emergency
record.locator: Preparation, closed-door outage estimates and discard guidance
record.support_scope: Thermometers and cold-source planning; refrigerator/freezer 4/48/24-hour estimates under the stated outage conditions; unsafe food may appear normal.

record.title: Food safety during power outage
record.support_scope: Food-specific discard/refreeze decisions and exceptions. Ice cream/frozen yogurt are discard entries even in the ice-crystal column; generic rules must not erase exceptions.

record.title: Survival kit supplies
record.support_scope: Three-day evacuation and two-week home supplies, easy-to-prepare food, sanitation supplies and a manual opener. Product quantities and household meal planning below are editorial applications.

record.title: Power outage safety
record.support_scope: Flashlights, electrical-needs planning, medical-provider advice, alerts and relocation when home conditions or medical power cannot be maintained.

record.title: Carbon monoxide safety
record.support_scope: Portable fuel generators outdoors at least 20 feet from structures; no indoor grills/camp stoves; alarms, installation and fresh-air/medical response.

record.title: Handwashing
record.support_scope: Soap and clean running water, 20-second scrub, rinse and dry; handwashing after toilet use and before food handling.

record.title: Emergency personal hygiene
record.locator: Temporary station, sanitizer limits and bathing
record.support_scope: Jug-based handwashing, at least 60% alcohol sanitizer when soap/water unavailable, limits with dirt/chemicals and authority-specific bathing advice.

record.title: Stay connected
record.support_scope: Important numbers, at least two meeting places, out-of-town contact and multiple communication routes; texts may succeed when calls do not.

record.title: Weather radio receivers
record.support_scope: Weather broadcasts require compatible VHF reception on 162.400-162.550 MHz; a plain AM/FM radio does not provide that capability.

record.title: Food safety during emergencies
record.support_scope: Virginia corroboration for appliance thermometers, closed-door estimates, cold-source planning and no taste testing.

record.title: Sewage backups
record.locator: What to do first and prevention
record.support_scope: Stop household water use during a sewage backup; contact the responsible service. Do not flush wipes or other trash. This provider is an example source, not the household’s confirmed utility.

record.title: Drinking water advisories
record.support_scope: Follow actual advisory uses/restrictions; appliance water filters do not override a boil advisory. Do not use connected refrigerator water/ice during advisories.

record.title: Safe generator use
record.support_scope: Running/starting requirements, professional transfer equipment, no outlet backfeeding, safe rated connections and cooling before refueling. No DIY wiring procedure is supplied.

record.title: Food and water safety during power outages and floods
record.locator: Power outages: warning after restored-power discussion
record.support_scope: Inadequately refrigerated or frozen perishable food can cause illness even after thorough cooking. Used for this warning only; FoodSafety.gov item tables govern this core’s food decisions, not the FDA page’s broader temperature statements.

record.title: Bleach treatment
record.guidance: Use the concentration-specific EPA table; for clear water use eight drops of 6% or six of 8.25% bleach per gallon. Double for cloudy, colored or very cold water after settling/prefiltration; wait 30 minutes. If no slight chlorine odor, repeat dose and wait 15 more minutes. Do not infer precise milliliters from an arbitrary dropper.

record.title: Calcium hypochlorite
record.guidance: EPA describes a heaping teaspoon of high-test calcium hypochlorite in two gallons to make stock, then one part stock to 100 parts water (one pint per 12.5 gallons). Follow product suitability and oxidizer precautions; do not adopt the book’s inconsistent ounce-per-three-quarts shortcut.

record.title: Iodine limits
record.guidance: Use only a defined product and label protocol. CDC cautions against iodine for pregnancy, thyroid conditions or iodine hypersensitivity and use beyond a few weeks. Do not rely on iodine for all parasites; it is not the default household long-term treatment.

record.title: Emergency boiling
record.guidance: Use CDC’s rolling boil: one minute, or three minutes above 6,500 feet, then cool and protect from recontamination. This controls germs and does not remove chemical hazards. EPA’s displayed altitude threshold differs (5,000 feet and an inconsistent metric equivalent); this dataset explicitly adopts CDC’s threshold, with local health instructions taking precedence.

record.title: Container sanitation and storage
record.guidance: Use CDC’s wash/sanitize/fill/close method and six-month replacement interval for home-filled water. A sealed lid and one bleach dose do not establish indefinite safe storage. Keep container sanitation solution separate from drinking-water dosing.

record.title: Pools are nonpotable reserves
record.guidance: Use pool water only for appropriate non-drinking purposes; normal pool maintenance does not make a drinking-water supply.

record.title: Rainfall arithmetic and reliability
record.guidance: US liquid gallon is 231 cubic inches: gallons = horizontal square feet × rainfall inches × 144 / 231. Thus 850 × 23 gives 12,187.012987 gallons/year, 33.389077/day gross; 2,000 × 23 gives 28,675.324675/year. The book’s 6,452-gallon reference is inconsistent. Subtract first flush, collection losses and overflow and model dry periods; annual yield divided by 365 is not dependable daily supply.

record.title: Virginia rainwater law
record.guidance: Virginia allows potable rainwater under Tier 4 requirements. Check system applicability, construction and operation permits, testing and building/local requirements. The reviewed design rule requires first flush but does not state four inches; the claimed general tax credit was not substantiated and remains unresolved.

record.title: Well sanitary completion
record.guidance: Use an approved class-specific casing, screen, grout and wellhead design; a buried plastic bag and tamped mud do not establish sanitary protection. Required testing and inspection still apply.

record.title: Dowsing
record.guidance: Use hydrogeologic investigation and testing. Do not rely on crossing rods to establish groundwater depth, quantity or quality.

record.title: Relative humidity
record.guidance: At fixed vapor content, warming lowers relative humidity and cooling raises it. Dew requires an adequately cold surface; fog interception is a separate mechanism. Neither high relative humidity alone nor morning sunlight establishes harvest yield.

record.title: Greywater controls
record.guidance: Treat greywater as potentially contaminated. Use approved separate systems and use-specific treatment, bypass and backflow protections; Virginia’s cited residential provisions limit untreated tank storage to 24 hours. Do not use untreated shower water for dishes or treat any outdoor discharge as automatically lawful.

record.title: Potable reuse
record.guidance: Potable reuse needs purpose-designed treatment, monitoring and applicable approvals. Conventional wastewater effluent and household distilled urine are not established safe drinking-water sources by these descriptions.

record.title: Food during a power outage
record.guidance: Keep refrigerator/freezer doors closed, monitor time and temperature, and follow CDC discard guidance. An unopened refrigerator normally gives four hours; full and half-full freezers approximately 48 and 24 hours respectively. Do not taste food for safety or preserve food that has become unsafe.

record.title: Water treatment and chemical limits
record.guidance: Use CDC rolling-boil guidance: one minute, or three above 6500 feet, then cool and protect. Boiling and disinfection do not remove toxic chemicals. Match any disinfectant to product, concentration, water condition and label contact time. CDC and EPA currently display different high-altitude thresholds; this examination explicitly uses CDC. No generic filter or silver additive is endorsed.

record.title: Stored safe water
record.guidance: Use safe water and sanitized suitable food-grade containers; keep closed, cool, shaded and dated. CDC recommends replacing home-filled water every six months. Container sanitation solution and drinking-water dosing are different procedures.

record.title: Combustion indoors
record.guidance: CO is invisible and odorless. Outdoor-only stoves, lanterns, grills and generators must not become indoor appliances merely because a window is open. Generators belong outdoors more than 20 feet from openings. Use correctly installed vented equipment and battery-backed CO alarms. Never heat a home with a gas oven.

record.title: Medical claims
record.guidance: Keep wounds clean with soap and safe water and covered; obtain urgent assessment for infection or serious injury. Historical honey, herbs, alcohol, steam and surgical-tool lists are not validated treatments or sterile procedures. This examination does not supply diagnoses, dosing or DIY surgery instructions.

record.title: Rated lifting equipment
record.guidance: Use ladders only for designed purposes and lifting gear within its identified working-load ratings. A ladder, tie-down strap, improvised tripod or tree branch is not an approved hoist simply because it appears sturdy. OSHA sources provide safety constraints; applicability to a particular homeowner operation is not determined.

record.title: Stew must not use the book’s water-bath process
record.guidance: Reject the page 43-45 stew process. Low-acid combinations require an appropriate tested pressure-canning recipe and all ingredient, jar, altitude and canner controls. NCHFP soup guidance excludes thickeners, dairy, rice and pasta. A vacuum seal does not prove safe processing; do not improvise a pressure-canning substitution for arbitrary stew.

record.title: Unsafe raw-meat sun drying
record.guidance: Reject uncontrolled multi-day raw-meat drying and brittle texture as proof of safety. Use a validated jerky process with controlled meat handling, heating and drying; NCHFP gives a 160 F internal-temperature control and specific methods. No blanket shelf-life or parasite-kill promise is adopted.

record.title: Pickles need a tested recipe
record.guidance: Use tested food/vinegar/water proportions, specified acidity and processing/storage directions. Do not dilute vinegar arbitrarily or assume hot filling followed by room-temperature storage is safe. Fermented products also require controlled salt and conditions.

record.title: Rainwater is not automatically potable
record.guidance: Test and treat for actual microbial and chemical hazards; generic filters or boiling alone may be insufficient. Keep potable and nonpotable piping protected. Virginia potable rainwater systems require applicable construction/operation approvals, with specific rain-barrel exclusions for other systems.

record.title: Ferrocement construction not validated
record.guidance: The book supplies no structural thickness, reinforcement calculation, strength test, certified contact materials or complete potable design. Mortar ratios and one week of curing do not establish a safe tank. Obtain qualified design and suitable materials.

record.title: Silver additives not validated
record.guidance: No validated silver dose, contact time or complete water-safety protocol is provided. Do not ingest improvised colloidal-silver preparations or equate this proposal with a certified treatment device. NCCIH documents ingestion harms; it does not evaluate every silver-containing water product.

record.title: Dowsing is not a reliable well investigation
record.guidance: Use geological and hydrological investigation and water testing to establish likely depth, yield and quality. Rod movement or claimed intuition does not supply those measurements.

record.title: Well shafts require qualified protective design
record.guidance: Do not enter a hand-dug shaft using this chapter as a safety plan. Improvised timber rings, taper and masonry replacement do not establish collapse protection. Atmospheric hazards, access, rescue, rated rigging and compliant sanitary completion need independent professional assessment.

record.title: Avoid flame-based security lighting
record.guidance: Fires near windows, elevated torches and unattended perimeter flames create ignition and exposure hazards. Use safe nonflame lighting, observation, escape plans and emergency assistance.

record.title: Cooling must fit climate and airflow design
record.guidance: Direct evaporation cools by adding moisture and is most useful in dry air. The proposed solar chimney does not demonstrate a coherent cooled-supply/exhaust path, reliable draft or humid-climate comfort. Site-specific design and measurements are required; overheating needs a separate safe response plan.

record.title: Do not improvise flue distribution
record.guidance: Use the approved appliance and chimney configuration, required clearances and qualified inspection. Long or room-to-room exhaust pipes are not a generic heat exchanger; poor draft, creosote and CO can result. The EPA Burn Wise page is archived guidance, not current installation code.

record.title: Seasoning time is not a moisture measurement
record.guidance: Store suitable firewood off the ground with covered top and ventilated sides; verify moisture with a meter, below 20% in EPA guidance. Six to twelve months alone does not prove dry fuel.

record.title: Bucket waste is not approved garden compost
record.guidance: The cited Virginia rule requires NSF Standard 41 certification for composting toilets and directs removed material to burial, not vegetable gardens or ground surface. Do not assume a covered bucket, lack of odor or elapsed time provides pathogen reduction or approval. Consult VDH for applicable approved sanitation and other wastewater arrangements.

record.title: CO is not visible smoke
record.guidance: Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless. Smoke appearance cannot reveal its presence or absence; appropriate alarms, safe appliance placement and venting are needed.

record.title: Canning needs a tested process, not merely a seal
record.guidance: Reject 158 F for 20 minutes as a universal sterilization rule. Low-acid home-canned food needs an appropriate tested pressure-canning process. Follow the exact food, formulation, preparation, pack, jar, headspace, time, pressure and altitude requirements. A pop, concave lid or intact seal does not prove adequate processing. No arbitrary recipe is made safe by substituting an invented pressure-canning time.

record.title: Jars, failed seals and pressure-canner operation
record.guidance: Use the selected tested process and equipment/lid directions. Where empty-jar presterilization is required, NCHFP specifies boiling water and elevation adjustment; 158 F is inadequate as the stated method. Pressure canners need ten minutes of free steam venting, correct altitude-adjusted operation, full processing time and natural cooling. If pressure drops, restart the full time. Seal failure requires prompt appropriate handling; eligible reprocessing uses a new lid and full correct process within 24 hours. This is not a rescue rule for initially unsafe food.

record.title: Drying is not a substitute for validated heating and endpoints
record.guidance: Use food-specific tested preparation, heating, drying and storage directions. Uncontrolled raw-meat sun drying and a 155 F air setting do not establish a safe internal heat treatment. Refrigerate jerky marination; do not infer a microbial kill from dryness, firmness or color. Outdoor sun drying is limited to suitable foods and favorable weather, rather than all meat and vegetables. Jerky shelf life cannot be inferred from the author’s months-long anecdote.

record.title: Salt-fish procedure has unresolved controls
record.guidance: The source omits a measured food-grade salt formulation, fish-specific handling, safe holding temperature, drying endpoint and validated keeping conditions. Rock or ice-cream-maker salt is not established as suitable for food by that description. The reviewer has not supplied a replacement salt-fish recipe; obtain a tested fish-specific method before use.

record.title: Reject oven dry canning
record.guidance: Do not use the book’s lidded-jar, twelve-hour oven process or reheat failed seals as a preservation method. NCHFP does not recommend oven or dry canning. Independently, the unit conversion is wrong: (200-32) times 5/9 is about 93.3 C, not 70 C. The author’s own lack-of-proof warning does not validate the procedure.

record.title: Pickles and ferments require food-specific controls
record.guidance: Retain tested food-to-liquid proportions and the recipe’s specified vinegar acidity, salt, temperature, fermentation completion, processing and storage requirements. Do not use tanginess or submersion alone as a safety test. The seven book ferments lack adequate process specifications; a small cabbage count is not a weight-based salt formulation. For comparison, F08 uses three tablespoons of salt per five pounds of shredded cabbage and describes about three to four weeks at 70-75 F, with its full handling and storage directions still required. This is a separate tested method, not a validated edit of the book recipe. The five quick-pickle recipes omit essential controls. Pickled eggs must be refrigerated; no recommended home-canning method makes these eggs pantry-stable.

record.title: Smoking and curing do not automatically make shelf-stable meat
record.guidance: Use a validated food-specific cure and process, the correct measured curing product and dose, refrigerated handling, an internal food thermometer and appropriate post-process storage. A premix is not self-dosing. Smoker-air temperature, dark color, a supposed impermeable pellicle or re-smoking a cut surface cannot demonstrate safety. USDA’s reviewed smoking-storage excerpt directs refrigeration within two hours, use within four days or freezing. No complete alternative shelf-stable curing recipe is supplied here.

record.title: Oxygen-reduced packaging is only for suitable dry foods
record.guidance: Do not equate absence of oxygen with absence of microbial hazards. USU warns about botulism with moist food in reduced-oxygen packages and describes about 10% or less moisture for this dry-storage context. That limit alone does not certify every product or a universal shelf life. Use known suitable food-contact containers, a food-appropriate packaging specification, clean equipment and manufacturer-sized absorbers. White color, a rat anecdote, a vacuum-cleaner hose or a nominal absorber size is not validation.

record.title: Measure cold storage and match the crop
record.guidance: A root cellar or evaporative cooler is not a refrigerator unless measured conditions support the food’s requirements. VCE calls for refrigerated food below 40 F; a 55 F claim is inadequate for general perishables. Match produce variety, humidity, temperature, curing and ventilation rather than treating the chart’s durations as guarantees. F15 describes very moist apple and pear storage rather than the book’s undefined medium humidity. UMN gives around 50-55 F for winter squash and pumpkins. The older WSU bulletin itself has different generalized and crop-specific squash ranges; these are not interchangeable universal prescriptions. Freezer burn concerns quality; it does not by itself make food unsafe.

record.title: Shelf life and date labels are conditional
record.guidance: Most commercial date labels concern quality, with infant formula an exception. Proper storage and the actual product matter. No seal or date establishes perpetual safety. For home-canned food, authoritative labeling, storage and best-quality guidance should be used instead of the book’s indefinite-life reassurance.

record.title: Avoid blanket anti-preservative and untested-GMO claims
record.guidance: FDA describes both antimicrobial and antioxidant preservative functions, rather than a merely cosmetic role. FDA, EPA and USDA have regulatory roles for genetically engineered foods, including FDA’s voluntary product-by-product consultation and submitted safety assessment data. These sources do not support the book’s blanket size-based harm argument or absence-of-assessment claim.

record.title: Underground storage sketches are not construction plans
record.guidance: Excavation, earth loads, drainage, access, structural support, materials and entrapment hazards remain unresolved. A block lining or buried refrigerator sketch is not evidence of a safe structure. Obtain a qualified site-specific design before construction; this examination does not determine permits or code compliance.

record.title: Home-rendered lard shelf stability is not established
record.guidance: The source supplies no validated moisture endpoint, process specification or storage study. Pale color does not resolve that gap. No universal room-temperature shelf life is assigned. Obtain a tested rendering and storage method, or qualified food-preservation advice; this examination does not assert that all properly rendered lard requires refrigeration.

record.title: Identification must establish the actual specimen
record.guidance: Common names, resemblance, an app, odor, a single feature, a photograph or confidence do not establish a safe meal. Learn complete local identification and toxic lookalikes with qualified help; reject uncertain specimens. Assess exact species, plant part, maturity and preparation. A small taste cannot clear unknown plants or demonstrate absence of allergy. None of this examination’s plant profiles is an approved field identification key.

record.title: No universal clean-site shortcut
record.guidance: Assess land use, treatment history, contamination and water/soil conditions. Uphill position, neglected growth, washing and a 100-foot road setback do not demonstrate toxin-free plants. EPA’s lead guidance concerns actual testing and exposure controls, not certification of every roadside or urban forage site.

record.title: Medicinal claims remain unvalidated
record.guidance: Food use, traditional use and laboratory activity are not proof of clinical efficacy or a safe medicinal dose. NCCIH finds no compelling dandelion efficacy evidence and inconsistent red-clover findings for several promoted uses. NCI does not support these foods/herbs as cancer treatment. Other specific herbal claims here were screened for gaps, not each exhaustively searched in clinical literature. Do not replace appropriate medical care with them; clinician review must address diagnosis, interactions, dose, age and pregnancy. No pediatric wine, wound poultice, botanical antibiotic or oral treatment has been approved by this examination.

record.title: Poisoning, bleeding and eye-treatment claims require proper care
record.guidance: Daylily juice is not an established arsenic antidote. In suspected poisoning, seek poison-control or emergency help without waiting for symptoms; do not use a homemade antidote. Internal bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage and serious cardiac symptoms need urgent clinical evaluation rather than herbal dosing. CDC identifies heavy postpartum bleeding and serious maternal heart symptoms as urgent warning signs. Homemade rose tea is not a sterile eye medicine; FDA requires ophthalmic medicines to be sterile. These constraints address particular claims; the reviewer does not claim to have validated every medical condition in this book.

record.title: Plantain does not replace snakebite care
record.guidance: Get medical help immediately for suspected venomous snakebite. CDC advises against folk therapies and attempts to remove venom. Reject plantain poultices and juice as an antidote; do not delay care to gather or prepare herbs.

record.title: Cyanogenic plants and unassessed plant parts
record.guidance: Chokecherry stems, leaves and seeds have cyanogenic hazards; the book’s bark remedies and incomplete human warning must remain held. The stated many-small-seeds description also needs botanical reconciliation rather than serving as a key. Bamboo needs species-appropriate preparation, including discarding cooking water under the cited FSANZ guidance. Its reassurance about commercial canned shoots does not endorse arbitrary home canning or raw shoot juice. Serviceberry seed tea and other nonfruit medicinal uses remain unassessed; no universal safe part or dose is inferred.

record.title: Mushroom shortcuts and cooking guarantees fail
record.guidance: Require expert identification of each mushroom; a hollow interior, white flesh, cap color, lack of gills or cooking alone cannot certify safety. FDA reports illness associated with true morels and says cooking cannot guarantee safety. False-morel toxins can persist after cooking. No mushroom entry in this book is promoted to a validated consumption protocol.

record.title: Correct scale, illustration and range errors
record.guidance: Plantain flowering stems are not seven to twenty feet tall; the consulted Extension description says under twelve inches. The Typha figure visibly labels Carex typhina, a different plant, and is unsuitable as its range map. The burdock map URL and common-name scope require reconciliation with the Arctium lappa heading. The canna page contains stray layout letters. Range shading, broad ornamental distributions and this book’s incomplete keys do not demonstrate wild food availability in Virginia. Original details remain preserved rather than silently repaired.

record.title: Preparation and storage need complete methods
record.guidance: Use food-specific validated handling, detoxification, cooking, drying, fermentation and storage instructions. The acorn schedules, below-70-F wet holding, two-year storage, three-month tigernut drying and blanket herb-oil/fermentation advice are not validated processes. Bitterness, floating, sprouting, firmness or a calendar duration are not general safety tests. Cattail gluten/allergen claims and cooking-as-a-guarantee against tuber gas are unsupported. No replacement recipe or cellar construction is supplied.

record.title: Wild invertebrates are not automatically food
record.guidance: Identify an appropriate edible species, assess contamination and allergy, and use a validated food-specific preparation. Broad references to grubs, beetles, worms and ants are insufficient. Snail purging does not establish pathogen elimination; CDC warns against raw/undercooked snails and slugs in affected areas. That warning does not establish Virginia prevalence or a universal cooking schedule.

record.title: Maple syrup concentrates sap
record.guidance: Reject the instruction to add thirty-five parts water to one part sap. Extension describes evaporating water from collected sap to a controlled syrup endpoint. Tree and season affect yields; use tree-safe tapping and suitable food-contact equipment. A V-shaped wound, makeshift can-lid spile and thickness-by-eye are not the cited complete method. Sap-to-syrup yield ratios are not added-water recipes.

record.title: Willow is not risk-free aspirin
record.guidance: Defined willow-bark preparations have salicylate-related restrictions, interactions and gastrointestinal adverse effects. EMA excludes children/adolescents and third-trimester pregnancy for the assessed medicines. This does not validate chewing Salix alba leaves during childbirth or its use as a universal safe food. Do not substitute wild bark/leaves for a standardized medicine.

record.title: Virginia access differs by land manager
record.guidance: Get landowner permission and check current site-specific collection rules. The current Virginia park rule permits personal or individual collection of edible fruits, berries, fungi and nuts, while otherwise prohibiting taking or damaging vegetation except authorized scientific collecting. This exception does not authorize uprooting plants, stripping bark or tapping trees. The DCR search excerpt omitted this exception; this examination uses the actual Administrative Code text. DWR’s older WMA summary is context, not a current property authorization. Verify the exact land manager, activity and any site restrictions.

record.title: Economic narrative is not a forecast
record.guidance: Keep historical anecdotes, incomplete statistics and undated predictions separate from current planning. No imminent depression, universal recession duration, global depression count, automatic interest-rate surge or individual fortune is verified. Fed history describes policy and banking dynamics rather than one simple cause. General-purpose credit cards arose after the Great Depression according to the Smithsonian excerpt; earlier merchant credit must not be confused with modern bank cards. Inflation-adjusted fortunes and selected success stories do not establish ordinary attainable returns.

record.title: Emergency liquidity and debt need household-specific decisions
record.guidance: Choose a feasible reserve goal based on actual expenses and risks; a fixed six-month-income target is not universal. Review contract rates, essential bills, minimum payments, secured-debt consequences and accessible reserves before directing extra debt payments or selling major assets. High-yield labels and interest accrual do not guarantee inflation protection. FDIC’s reviewed primary excerpt states coverage of 250000 dollars per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category; verify institution, account and limits before assuming coverage. The excerpt does not certify any account or investment.

record.title: Business ideas need net-cost and demand checks
record.guidance: No side hustle, asset rental, passive-income operation or homemade product has guaranteed earnings. Account for startup cost, labor, transport, failure, taxes, licenses, insurance and sustained demand. FTC warns most legitimate-MLM participants earn little or nothing, with some losing money; product enthusiasm is insufficient. Cashless work is not automatically outside tax rules. No actual business feasibility study or individual earning forecast was performed.

record.title: Reject universal investment rankings
record.guidance: Assess objective, horizon, loss tolerance, diversification, fees, liquidity, tax and product-specific risks. Mutual funds vary; some offer low-cost broad diversification and all still have risk. Bonds, annuities, property, cash, collectibles and other categories are not uniformly best or worst. Interest-bearing cash need not preserve real purchasing power. Avoid interpreting market timing, a future rebound, contract wording or tangible-goods utility as guaranteed recovery or principal protection. No individualized portfolio or current transaction recommendation is provided.

record.title: Barter and home sales retain legal and tax constraints
record.guidance: IRS requires applicable fair-market-value barter income reporting; keep suitable records and determine filing obligations. Virginia home-food sales are subject to food rules with limited conditional exemptions, not a blanket permission for all preserves and sauces. Check applicable food, product, transport, childcare, alcohol/tobacco and other trade restrictions before offering services or goods.
